image_description: A close-up, side-profile view of a Rock Beauty fish (Holocanthus tricolor). The fish displays the characteristic black anterior body and head, transitioning to a bright yellow/gold posterior body. A distinct white vertical bar separates the black and yellow regions near the gill cover. The dorsal fin is visible along the top edge, appearing continuous. The background is a blurry, dark underwater environment.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The mouth area is either out of frame or obscured by the angle and resolution; 'brush-like teeth' are microscopic and impossible to verify at this resolution.
A large eye is clearly visible on the left side of the image, consistent with the species' anatomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Laterally compressed disc-shaped body with compact proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible portion of the body shows a high, laterally compressed profile typical of angelfish/butterflyfish.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Striking gold and black coloration: anterior body and head black, posterior body and tail golden yellow with black margin.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image clearly shows the black head/anterior section and the yellow posterior section. The specific 'black margin' on the tail is not fully visible as the tail is cut off, but the primary color block pattern is correct.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Continuous dorsal fin with spiny anterior and soft-rayed posterior portions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The dorsal fin runs continuously along the back. While individual spines vs rays are hard to distinguish due to resolution, the structural continuity is present.
The ventral side of the fish is largely obscured by shadow and the bottom edge of the frame, making the anal fin difficult to assess clearly.
The tail (caudal fin) is mostly outside the right edge of the frame.

There is significant blur that seems inconsistent with a standard depth-of-field; some edges of the fish blend into the background slightly unnaturally (edge bleeding).
